cse-2018-ga-7.approach: Rewrite each condition as a positive power and chain the substitutions back to p.

steps.title: Invert
steps.body: $p^{-x} = \frac1q \Rightarrow p^x = q$; similarly $q^y = r$ and $r^z = p$.

steps.title: Chain
steps.body: $p = r^z = (q^y)^z = \left((p^x)^y\right)^z = p^{xyz}$.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.body: $p^{xyz} = p^1 \Rightarrow xyz = 1$ (for $p \neq 0, \pm1$, which the general statement intends).

optionAnalysis.reason: $xyz = -1$ would give $p^{-1} = p$, not true in general.
$\frac{1}{pqr}$ is not an exponent obtainable from the chain.
Correct: $p^{xyz} = p \Rightarrow xyz = 1$.
$pqr$ mixes the bases into the exponent — no basis.

cse-2018-ga-7.verification: Take logs: $x = \frac{\ln q}{\ln p}$, $y = \frac{\ln r}{\ln q}$, $z = \frac{\ln p}{\ln r}$; product $= 1$.

cse-2018-ga-9.approach: Use the triangle angle sums of triangles AEB and ADF to express the two angles, then use the angle sum of quadrilateral ABCD.

steps.title: Triangle AEB
steps.body: $\angle DEC = \angle AEB$ (same angle at E), so $\angle DEC = 180^\circ - \angle BAD - \angle ABC$.

steps.title: Triangle ADF
steps.body: $\angle BFC = \angle AFD$ (same angle at F), so $\angle BFC = 180^\circ - \angle BAD - \angle ADC$.

steps.title: Add
steps.body: $\angle DEC + \angle BFC = 360^\circ - 2\angle BAD - (\angle ABC + \angle ADC)$.

steps.title: Quadrilateral ABCD
steps.body: $\angle BAD + \angle ABC + \angle BCD + \angle ADC = 360^\circ \Rightarrow \angle ABC + \angle ADC = 360^\circ - \angle BAD - \angle BCD$. Substituting: $\angle DEC + \angle BFC = 360^\circ - 2\angle BAD - 360^\circ + \angle BAD + \angle BCD = \angle BCD - \angle BAD$.

optionAnalysis.reason: Correct: derived from the triangle and quadrilateral angle sums.
$\angle BAD + \angle BCF$: $\angle BCF = 180^\circ - \angle BCD$, giving $180^\circ + \angle BAD - \angle BCD$, which differs in general.
$\angle BAD + \angle BCD$ has the wrong sign on $\angle BAD$.
$\angle CBA + \angle ADC = 360^\circ - \angle BAD - \angle BCD$, not the required sum.

cse-2018-ga-9.shortcut: Exterior angles: in triangle CDE, $\angle BCD = \angle DEC + \angle CDE$ (EC extended to B); in triangle ADF, $\angle CDE = \angle BAD + \angle BFC$ (AD extended to E). So $\angle BCD = \angle DEC + \angle BFC + \angle BAD$.
cse-2018-ga-9.verification: Both methods give $\angle DEC + \angle BFC = \angle BCD - \angle BAD$; this is the dart (arrowhead) rule for A-E-C-F.
